national.label: U.S. annual average transportation spending, 2025
national.unit: Mean per consumer unit, including vehicle purchases, fuel, insurance and transit
national.warning: A nationwide household-spending average is NOT the current price of a car, commute, toll, transit trip or a typical local household.

method.disclosure: Standardized price comparison: five weekdays per week, two paid transit fares per commuting day, OR one qualifying charged toll crossing per day. 52 weeks / 12 months. These are separately priced alternatives, NOT a combined commute or actual household quote. No inferred route, fare eligibility, fuel, parking, gas, tax, maintenance, insurance or congestion discounts.
method.important: Monthly fares are standardized arithmetic illustrations, not surveyed average passenger bills. A listed monthly pass is its own 30-day fare product; it is not calculated from the per-ride figure.

regions.name: New York City & northern New Jersey
regions.summary: See published NYC subway, PATH and NY-bound Port Authority crossing charges, then compare service and toll-system accountability.

rows.shortNote: $35 OMNY rolling seven-day cap; typical 10 paid weekday fares do not trigger it. Eligible transfers do not cost extra.

rows.tripType: 2 separately paid PATH fares per commute day
rows.shortNote: PATH's $131.50 30-day unlimited product is a distinct option. PATH and MTA are separate fare systems.

rows.tripType: 2 paid express fares per commute day
rows.shortNote: Illustration applies the listed $67 eligible seven-day express fare cap, not a single-fare multiplication.

rows.tripType: 1 charged New York-bound crossing per commute day
rows.shortNote: Class 1; qualifying NY/NJ E-ZPass; no Port Authority crossing toll on the westbound trip into NJ.

rows.tripType: 1 qualifying NY-bound off-peak crossing per commute day
rows.shortNote: Off-peak only; compare the actual travel time and conditions.

rows.tripType: 1 charged NY-bound crossing per commute day

rows.tripType: 1 eligible peak charge per commute day

Actual parking charges and vehicle ownership costs are not inferred from ZIP.

regions.name: National context / compare available regions
regions.summary: No nationwide standard subway fare or road toll exists. The cited NY/NJ and Chicago rates are examples, not prices inferred for your location.
missing: For a new state, a verified local operator and fare-zone table must be joined before displaying a price.
Nationwide agency performance and state-of-good-repair data exist, but the result cannot be assigned to your ZIP without matching its transit system.

sourceRules: Prices are unchanged from the original transport-fares-v1.json data file and retain its links and effective dates.
Do not aggregate mutually exclusive Port Authority E-ZPass and Tolls by Mail rates.
Do not combine separately priced subway/rail/toll examples into a claimed route without verified trip and transfer data.
Fare caps apply only to eligible service, card/device and time windows; compare simple weekday single-fare illustration and separate monthly passes without pretending they are equivalent periods.
Published rates and modeled paid-trip frequency are not observed local spending or proof that a toll or fare increase raised a given household's expenses.
Evidence of contracting waste or billing errors does not determine the dollar amount of any fare increase.
